description: Mapper-coverage breadth, sampled from the 758 .nes files under SubProjects/65-o-borked/bin/Debug/net8.0/roms (the 2847-file count in that folder includes the .chr/.prg/.ines side files). One representative title per mapper. The corpus is NOT in the repo and is NOT redistributable, so these cases SKIP on a machine that does not have it.
howChosen: Every .nes file's iNES header was read and grouped by mapper id. 25 distinct mappers are present: 0,1,2,3,4,5,7,9,11,13,34,41,47,64,66,67,68,69,71,79,113,118,119,228,232. Windows/NesEmulator/board/Cartridge.cs implements 0,1,2,3,4,5,7,9,30,33,90,228 - so 9 of the corpus's mappers are runnable and 16 are not. All 16 are listed below as explicit skip entries with the reason, so they are visible rather than silently dropped; mappers 30, 33 and 90 are implemented but have no representative in this corpus (30 is covered by cases/mapper30.json).

cases.description: Mapper 0 (NROM). Super Mario Bros. - the most-exercised NES program there is.
Mapper 1 (MMC1). The Legend of Zelda - battery-backed WRAM plus MMC1 serial register writes.
Mapper 2 (UNROM). Mega Man - CHR-RAM, bus-conflict-free PRG banking.
Mapper 3 (CNROM). Arkanoid - CHR-ROM bank switching only.
Mapper 4 (MMC3). Super Mario Bros. 3 - the scanline-IRQ workhorse, and the ROM the SMB3 red-clouds APU/PRG-bank bug was found and fixed on. The single most valuable non-FIX-specific case here.

Mapper 5 (MMC5, partial in this emulator). Castlevania III. Only 3 distinct colours at frame 600, so this case is weaker evidence than the others - it mostly proves MMC5 still loads and does not crash.
Mapper 7 (AxROM). Battletoads - single-screen mirroring and famously timing-sensitive code.
Mapper 9 (MMC2). Punch-Out!! - CHR latch tile-fetch trickery, driven by PPU reads rather than CPU writes, so it is a PPU-timing case as much as a mapper case.
Mapper 228. Action 52 - a multicart mapper, and the only >100 mapper id this emulator implements that the corpus has a sample of.
SMB3 on the FMC stack, as a cross-check that mapper-4 behaviour is being compared across two core families rather than only one.
